summary: The patch adds a defensive `iscoroutine` check in `get_response_async`, but this runs AFTER the outermost (first) middleware has already executed its `process_response`, so it does not stop that middleware from receiving a coroutine — the actual reported symptom. It fixes the wrong layer (boundary return value) instead of the root cause in `MiddlewareMixin`, which must await its async inner `get_response` before invoking `process_response`.

issues.description: Reported bug is that the first middleware's process_response() receives a coroutine. That call happens INSIDE _middleware_chain execution (the outermost middleware), before control returns to get_response_async. Conditionally awaiting the chain's return value cannot retroactively change what process_response already received. For the coroutine case, pre-patch `await chain(request)` and post-patch `iscoroutine → await` yield the identical final response, so the actual user-facing issue (e.g. django-cors-headers getting a coroutine) is not resolved. Root cause fix belongs in MiddlewareMixin (awa

Runtime `asyncio.iscoroutine()` branch is a band-aid that papers over indeterminate async-ness of the middleware chain rather than guaranteeing the chain is properly adapted. get_response_async should know deterministically whether the chain is a coroutine; a type-sniffing conditional signals the middleware adaptation layer is the real defect site.
